event.hazel_heart2.1.text: An almanac, eighty-one years old. Page two hundred and four: a snowdrop, still white. (The margins know more than the weather. I'm still reading them.)
event.hazel_heart2.1.why: hint: the margins thread, echoed not repeated

event.hazel_heart2.3.text: Beside it, in pencil: the first frost, guessed. They missed by three days. (People guessed, back then. Nobody guesses now. I find that odd.)
event.hazel_heart2.3.why: resister clocks the village's new exactness

event.hazel_heart2.3.text: Beside it, in pencil: the first frost, guessed. They missed by three days. (This year's almanac hedges. Even the weather is keeping quiet.)

event.hazel_heart4.intro.text: I'd like to trade. A book for a book. (An even trade. This village is very exact about trades. I keep the receipts.)
event.hazel_heart4.intro.why: the bargain's shadow as a trade custom

event.hazel_heart4.intro.text: I'd like to trade. A book for a book. (Even trades are a custom here. Older than the shelves.)

dlg.hazel.hiding.r0.text: Pages turning, two rooms away. Other people's thoughts, kept. (Kept things are this village's specialty. I shelve one kind.)

event.hazel_heart6.after.text: I checked your face just now. It stayed kind. (Lately I check everyone's. Some are too calm. I'm charting it.)
event.hazel_heart6.after.why: frightened: she charts the Keepers' calm

event.hazel_heart8.intro.text: Would you hear a thing I wrote? (I tried the gray cat. It watches the door now. Everyone's a critic.)
Would you hear a thing I wrote? (The gray cat left at line three. It leaves everywhere early, lately.)

event.hazel_heart10.intro.text: I'll read it for you. Just you. (Away from the window, please. We both read the same records.)
event.hazel_heart10.intro.why: revelation tier: shared knowledge, no speech

event.hazel_heart10.intro.text: I'll read it for you. Just you. (Quietly. Some nights this village listens back. We'll be quieter than it.)
event.hazel_heart10.intro.why: frightened band, echoes the hum thread

event.hazel_heart10.intro.text: I'll read it for you. Just you. (The shelves don't count. Lately they're the only audience I trust.)

event.hazel_friend.success.text: Perfect. One tart, then a knock on the borrower's door. (Doors open slower this season. A tart is good oil.)
event.hazel_friend.success.why: hushed village; borrower stays a living stranger

event.hazel_birthday.intro.text: It's my birthday. (I kept it quiet. The year is loud enough.) Please sit. There's enough for two.
event.hazel_birthday.intro.why: full-only shading; mild birthday stays cozy

dlg.hazel.partners.r2.text: The forest. With you. (The birds there have gone quiet. We'll lend them some noise.)

event.reading_night.poem.text: The lamp does not mind the dark. It keeps it company. It keeps—it keeps it company. ...That's the eleven. (One line minded the dark. I cut it.)
event.reading_night.poem.why: allowed short stammer; the poem flinches

event.festival_winter_lanterns.1.text: One lantern, one wish. Fold it small. (The sky has been attentive lately. Give it something kind.)
One lantern, one wish. Fold it small. (The dark is roomier this winter. Wishes have farther to go.)

event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l1.text: Your spring almanac. Third shelf. (The old ones all mark the same four nights. Yours should too.)
event.overheard_hazel_ione_1.l1.why: hint: four-dates thread, told to its co-keeper

event.overheard_dorian_hazel_1.l4.text: (The best kind.) Though even the jays going quiet is a kind of loud.
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_1.l4.why: answers his jays line with the ladder

event.overheard_dorian_hazel_3.l2.text: We could. (The window faces the forest. Lately the forest faces back. We'll sit anyway.)
event.overheard_dorian_hazel_3.l2.why: the woods seem closer; sitting anyway is the warmth

adds.text: (The window faces the wood. I shelve with my back to it. ...Habit.)
adds.why: a habit the player can wonder about

adds.text: A small poem. Six lines. (Short enough to keep safe. Long enough to mean it.)
(Every chair full, every lamp lit. I counted the windows anyway. Twice.)
(Four nights a year, every door shuts early. Tonight isn't one. I checked.)
adds.why: hint: the four-nights custom; no heart10 payoff

cuts.why: the laugh-at-line-four joke falls flat at frightened
